overview: Although its title refers to recognizing May 2025 as Renewable Fuels Month, the version of this resolution the House passed instead creates an "E-15 Rural Domestic Energy Council," appointed by the Speaker of the House. E-15 is gasoline blended with 15 percent ethanol, a fuel made mostly from corn. The council is directed to study the sale of E-15, U.S. refinery capacity, the Renewable Fuel Standard (the federal program requiring a certain amount of renewable fuel in the nation's fuel supply), the credits used to track compliance with it, market access, and federal regulations, and to propose legislation to Congress by February 15, 2026, with the aim of considering a bill by February 25, 2026. The House treated it as passed, as amended, on January 22, 2026.
for: Supporters say a dedicated council can bring farmers' and refiners' competing concerns together and produce concrete legislation on year-round E-15 sales and fuel rules on a fast timeline.
against: Critics say a House resolution cannot change fuel law on its own, and that a council appointed by one leader with a tight deadline may not fully weigh the views of everyone affected by fuel policy.
